horizon_growth.note: pooled over series x scored test origins per TRUE horizon h (direct per-h models) — the error-growth curve the horizon slider demonstrates

band_types.learner: p50 ± q80 split-conformal width per horizon, calibrated on the selection origins, zero-clipped and sorted
band_types.sparse: P(any sale) + quantile ladder of the training history (no collapsing band)

bands.note: per-h coverage/width are the committed pooled values over the scored test origins; per-series panels show the conformal p10/p90 (learner rows) or the P(sale)+ladder (sparse rows) instead

decision.label: order-up-to policy simulation — cost assumptions documented, no savings claims

cost_assumptions.cost_basis: per scored cell (series x test origin x horizon)

decision.mapping_note: order(origin, h, τ) = max(point forecast + offset, 0) with offset = quantile_map[class][policy][h][τ]; offsets are τ-quantiles of the policy's selection-origin residuals per (class, h) — the committed simulation's own τ→quantile mapping, recomputed on the re-run scores

headline.claim: the routed pipeline leads the multi-step leaderboard; routing lumpy series away from the boosted model wins +4.6 MAE [4.2, 5.1] over all-HGB (95% paired bootstrap over series x scored origins)

catalog_summary.shock_note: demand shock xs scales the last 7 days before the origin (the demand signal every candidate reads): statistical curves are re-fit on the shocked window, boosted curves re-predict through the fitted per-horizon trees on the shocked lag trio — precomputed offline, exact; bands stay on the unshocked base run
catalog_summary.routing_rule: sparse (ADI >= 1.32) series route to the best statistical method (zero/seasonal_naive/Croston/SBA/TSB) chosen per series on the selection origins ONLY; smooth/erratic series stay on the direct HGB

experiment_origins.cap_note: weekly origins, capped at 20 by dropping the oldest (exact weekly cadence kept) for runtime; the window starts the day AFTER the origin (no embargo gap)

evaluation_metadata.track: multi_step (primary); the top-level rolling_origin_holdout_v1 keys describe the retained frozen nowcast track

origins.cap_note: weekly origins, capped at 20 by dropping the oldest (exact weekly cadence kept) for runtime; the window starts the day AFTER the origin (no embargo gap)

evaluation_metadata.holdout_designation: last 4 origins = test (scored once); the earlier origins select (routing + conformal calibration) only
evaluation_metadata.selection_rule: per-series routing method = lowest summed |error| over the selection origins among zero/seasonal_naive/Croston/SBA/TSB; never reads test actuals (property-tested by shuffling the test origins' actuals)
evaluation_metadata.feature_semantics: direct per-horizon models: calendar of the target date + lags lag_h, lag_{h+7}, lag_{h+14} (>= h days old relative to the target — no actual within h days of the target is referenced); training rows use targets <= the origin only
evaluation_metadata.uncertainty: per-horizon split-conformal (learner rows) and P(sale)+quantile ladder (sparse rows), both calibrated on selection origins

metric_definitions.mae: mean |actual - forecast| over series x scored test origins at horizon h
metric_definitions.mase: pooled |err| / pooled per-series in-sample seasonal-naive-7 scale (zero-scale rows excluded)
metric_definitions.rmsse: M5-style: per-series sqrt(MSE(err)/MSE(in-sample seasonal-naive-7)), averaged over series (zero-scale excluded)
metric_definitions.pinball_pXX: mean pinball loss of the learner quantile at level XX
metric_definitions.coverage: share of actuals inside the per-h band on the scored origins
metric_definitions.calibration_verdict: |coverage - target| <= 0.05 -> calibrated; above -> conservative; below -> optimistic

evaluation_metadata.target_definition: The forecast target is the next 14 days of daily units per country-product series (top 8 countries x top 200 products by volume), aggregated from cleaned Online Retail II transactions (cancellations removed).
evaluation_metadata.nowcast_track_note: PRIMARY multi-step headline. The per-model blocks above are the retained frozen nowcast (one-day-ahead) track, rolling_origin_holdout_v1 — valid but never mixed into the multi-step leaderboard. Each multi-step row is a TRUE horizon-h forecast issued at the origin (no actual within h days of the target is referenced).

source.license: free for research (Chen, Gallino & Li 2012, Management Science)

dataset_metadata.cancellation_filtering: Sales lines only: rows with Quantity > 0 are kept; cancellations and returns (negative-quantity lines) are removed — returns are a separate business process and net-of-returns demand would double-count reverse logistics. Blank stock codes are dropped.
dataset_metadata.quantity_handling: Daily sum of line Quantity per (date, country, stock_code); the panel's 'units' column is that daily total (integer). 'price' is the mean line price of the day (carried for reference, not a model target).
dataset_metadata.geography: Top 8 countries by total unit volume are kept as 'stores'; all other countries are dropped.
dataset_metadata.products: Top 200 stock codes by total unit volume are kept as 'products'; the rest are dropped.
dataset_metadata.daily_aggregation: Transactions are aggregated to one row per (date, country, stock_code); the panel is reindexed to the complete daily calendar between the first and last observed dates, and missing day-series combinations are zero-filled (forward-filled price, 0 where never observed).
dataset_metadata.zero_sales_caveat: Zero-sales days may be missing rather than true zero demand: the source has no trading calendar, so a zero-filled day can mean 'closed or not trading' as easily as 'no demand'.
dataset_metadata.target_definition: The forecast target is the next 14 days of daily units per country-product series (top 8 countries x top 200 products by volume), aggregated from cleaned Online Retail II transactions (cancellations removed).

intermittency.method: Syntetos-Boylan quadrants: ADI (avg inter-demand interval) vs CV^2 (squared coefficient of variation) over each series' full history
intermittency.routing_rule: multi-step track: ADI >= 1.32 (intermittent + lumpy) series route to the best statistical method chosen on the selection origins only; smooth/erratic series use the direct per-horizon boosted model
